destination_poi.description_summer: Le Soliat is a popular hiking target on the rim of Creux du Van. Roads, farms and several inns characterise the wide high plain between Lac de Neuchâtel and Val de Travers. On the highest point there is a summit cross and a panoramic display protected against the grazing cattle by a wooden fence. In the area there is also an ibex colony.
destination_poi.description_winter: Le Soliat is a popular target on the rim of Creux du Van. Roads, farms and several inns characterize the wide high plain between Lac de Neuchâtel and Val de Travers. On the highest point there is a summit cross and a panoramic display protected against the grazing cattle by a wooden fence. In the area there is also an ibex colony. Please note the wildlife reserves in the northeastern part.

photos.caption: Dos d'Âne in profile, behind are the high plain of Vallée des Ponts, Mont Racine and Les Tablettes.
Depending on your choice of itinerary, you sometimes have to deal with trees.
On the way pleasurable bouldering exercises can be included.
On the upper, horizontal stretch of the ridge
The standard route merges from the left (red markings). However, the hiker prefers to scramble up the ridge.
If you like being exposed, choose to climb the pinnacles. However, descending sometimes is not that easy.
Sometimes the ridge is structured like stairs.
On the way to Le Soliat; to the left of the dry stone wall is the abyss. Attention: partly protection zone left of the beautiful stone wall!
View from Le Soliat to the Bernese Alps
On nice weekends Creux du Van is rather crowded.

segments.description: The start is at the Noiraigue train station, which hosts a quaint little tea room selling local products and furnishing information about the area. From the station follow the signposts down valley for a few steps and then cross the railway lines towards Creux du Van. After ca. 770 m branch off the road to take the forest path to Ferme Robert, a well-known inn.
segments.title: Noiraigue – Ferme Robert

segments.description: The start of Dos d'Âne is not easy to find. You have two possibilities: a) where the forest road bends left to reach the parking lot below Ferme Robert, on the right-hand side take a forest path going up the escarpment, then keep left to look for red markings. Or b) branch off the road at the lower building of Ferme Robert (accommodation) to traverse a pasture (pathless) and then a small water ditch. You reach a hidden pasture on three sides surrounded by forest. Traverse this pasture until you find a narrow passage through the trees (a few stones on the ground point at the passage). Now on a path with a few markings ascend a very steep and fairly tiresome, slippery slope with schrofen and some rocks. Beware of the rock fall! The Dos d’Âne ridge gets more and more distinct and rocky, while the slope is slightly less steep. The path and the markings are more and more visible. Further up, the ridge is almost horizontal. Follow the ridge line or slightly on the right-hand side (N). Some pinnacles are traversed, others bypassed. In general it is much hiking and some scrambling. After P. 1343 the ridge becomes less rocky before you meet Sentier des 14 Contours, which you follow up to P. 1374.
segments.title: Ferme Robert – P. 1374

segments.description: From the signpost follow the rim of Creux du Van. Attention: partly protection zone left of the beautiful stone wall! After about 20 minutes the trail turns right to lead up to the gentle knoll of Le Soliat.
segments.title: P. 1374 – Le Soliat

segments.description: From Le Soliat go back to the rim of Creux du Van to follow the distinct trail eastward. You pass a very attractive, mostly well-visited viewpoint, which offers an excellent and impressive view of the Creux du Van cirque. Continue on the trail until on the left-hand side the so called Sentier du Single branches off. It zig-zags down, sometimes steep, sometimes slippery, but always manageable (T2+) to reach P. 1197 and the bottom of the rock cirque. Now take one of the many trails back to Ferme Robert and Noiraigue.
segments.title: Le Soliat – Noiraigue

teaser: The Dos d'Âne (back of a donkey) is likely the most attractive itinerary to the popular Creux du Van: an entertaining hike with scrambling passages.
title: On the Dos d'Âne

Noiraigue–Ferme Robert 1 h
Ferme Robert–Le Soliat 2 h
Le Soliat–Ferme Robert 1 h
Ferme Robert–Noiraigue ¾ h

The hike is an entertaining itinerary on a ridge and through the forest with several scrambling passages. The T4 degree is for the lower part in the steep forest (fairly difficult orientation, tiresome terrain) and the upper, rocky part (easy scrambling passages). If the terrain is dry, the whole tour does not necessarily require hiking boots. Sturdy sneakers will do.
